Background execution and child processes

Android 12 and newer may end app child processes, and Termux may show signal 9. Some Android 14 and newer devices offer “Disable child process restrictions” in Developer options. Its name and availability depend on the system. Turning off Developer options may restore the restriction.

For long tasks, run termux-wake-lock to keep the CPU awake and termux-wake-unlock when finished. A wake lock increases battery use and does not remove child process limits or manufacturer background restrictions.
If a task stops in the background, check the Termux battery and background settings and keep its notification visible.
